source.title: Beyond Linear Superposition: Discovering Climate Features in AI Weather Models with KAN-SAE

record.tranche_reason: The study discusses polysemanticity and sparse feature representations, but its experiments measure SAE dictionary quality and climate features, not whether individual network neurons respond to unrelated inputs.
record.gate_note: The paper reports SAE-level comparisons in Table 1 and later sections, including feature utilization, redundancy, reconstruction fidelity, climate-feature localization, and steering. These do not measure individual neurons' polysemanticity or any of the claim versions' named behaviors. The table metrics are recorded as related findings with versions ["none"]; the feature case studies and steering results are not neuron-polysemanticity results.
record.test_reason: The paper builds on superposition/polysemanticity as motivation for SAEs and reports only its own SAE method's performance (KAN-SAE vs linear SAE) on a weather transformer's residual stream. It never measures whether individual neurons of SONNY or any other network respond to unrelated inputs, so no version is tested. T4 fits better than T6 because the finding is used as the premise for the tool.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also claim nonlinear activations are essential for interpretability of weather models. They also say circuit analysis shows features become more event-specific with depth. They note limits: one layer, one model, two phenomena, and an ad hoc alive threshold τ.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains KAN-SAE and linear SAE dictionaries on S ONNY weather-model activations; it does not reproduce the original neuron-response measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports comparisons between KAN-SAE and LIN-SAE; it does not test sensitivity of neuron-polysemanticity measurements to settings.

fits_no_version.finding: On SONNY Layer-5 residual activations, KAN-SAE has 95.2% alive features vs 55.5% for a ReLU SAE. Median inter-feature |r| is 0.076 vs 0.092, and explained variance is 84.2% vs 86.6%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Per-feature learnable B-spline encoder activations yield more alive, less redundant SAE features than a ReLU SAE on a weather transformer, at a small reconstruction cost.

record.problems: The paper's own conclusion notes that the analysis is restricted to Layer 5 of one model and two climate phenomena. Its evidence about feature utilization and redundancy concerns learned SAE features, not individual network neurons or their responses to unrelated inputs.
record.rows_left_out: Climate-feature case studies and steering results were omitted because they concern SAE latent features and forecast effects, not individual-neuron polysemanticity.

untested.parts: No neuron-level analysis of vision classifiers.
No MLP neuron analysis in language models; the residual stream of a weather transformer is probed via SAEs only.
Superposition is assumed as the SAE premise, not tested; neuron polysemanticity is not measured.
The activation function is varied in the SAE encoder, not in the model's neurons; no polysemantic-neuron share is reported.

record.verdict_notes: Polysemanticity is mentioned only in related work as motivation; the record's 'discusses' is closer to uses-as-premise (T4). The 'dead feature' and 'alive' metrics concern SAE latents, not network neurons. Climate case studies and steering rows are rightly left out.

versions.untested_parts: Individual neurons in image classifiers responding to unrelated visual inputs.
MLP neurons in transformer language models responding to unrelated tokens or contexts.
Whether neuron polysemanticity is caused by sparse features being packed together under capacity pressure.
Whether neuron polysemanticity arises without capacity pressure from initialization, regularization, or training noise.
The share of polysemantic neurons across network activation functions, architectures, or regularization settings, and performance costs of lowering that share.
Whether apparently mixed neuron responses are actually one shared feature or related jobs.
Whether neuron polysemanticity depends on activation range examined or explanation scoring.
